analysis_summaries: The repository contains a YOLO11s ONNX object detector trained on COCO and an application.py script described as a single-image sanity test. The script preprocesses an image by letterboxing it to 640×640, converting to RGB, and scaling pixel values to [0,1]. The model outputs raw bounding boxes and 80 class scores, which the decoder transposes, confidence-filters, and suppresses with NMS. The application identifies vehicle categories, but the scan does not establish video-file support or a DeepStream/TensorRT engine pipeline, so it cannot be confirmed to serve the requested video task as specified.

info.user_prompt: Build a real-time edge vision pipeline for CrossGuard Edge, a pedestrian and vehicle monitoring system for road crossings. Detect people, cars, buses, trucks, and motorcycles using an available pretrained object-detection model. Support a local video file as the input and a USB camera if supported. Use NVIDIA DeepStream and compile at least one model to a TensorRT engine. Display live annotated detections and generate JSON metadata or event output if supported. Complete the full PipeGen workflow and provide the TensorRT speed report. Prioritize a working, validated pipeline on my NVIDIA RTX 4060 Linux laptop. Do not invent performance measurements.

advice.text: At the camera: zoom in or move closer.
At the Model stage: a larger model input size helps small targets.

evidence: The view holds still between frames, so the camera looks fixed.

targets.basis: application.py identifies the selected ONNX model as COCO-pretrained, lists person in CLASS_NAMES, and describes output0 as box coordinates plus 80 class scores, decoded with transpose, confidence filtering and NMS. The ONNX metadata names also maps class 0 to person.
targets.output: YOLO11s produces bounding-box coordinates and class scores; the decoder maps detections to the COCO person label.

targets.basis: application.py explicitly defines VEHICLE_CLASSES as bicycle, car, motorcycle, bus, train, truck, and boat, and describes the model output as box coordinates plus 80 class scores. The selected ONNX metadata supplies the corresponding COCO class names.
targets.output: YOLO11s produces bounding-box coordinates and class scores for COCO classes; the decoder maps vehicle detections to bicycle, car, motorcycle, bus, train, truck, or boat.
